_comment: Firefox (Gecko) MV3 manifest. Differs from ../manifest.json in exactly four
places, all forced by Gecko and none of them cosmetic:
1. NO "key". That field is a Chromium mechanism for deriving a stable
extension ID from a public key. Gecko ignores it and AMO rejects
manifests carrying unknown top-level fields in strict validation, so it
is dropped rather than left inert.
2. "browser_specific_settings.gecko.id" replaces it. Without an explicit id
Firefox assigns a temporary one that changes on every reload, which
breaks storage.local persistence across restarts of a temporarily-loaded
add-on. Note this id is NOT the extension origin -- see point 4.
3. "background.scripts" instead of "background.service_worker". Gecko MV3
backgrounds are non-persistent event pages, not service workers. This is
also the only place compat.js can be loaded for the background context
on Firefox, because importScripts does not exist in an event page.
4. strict_min_version 115. scripting.executeScript with a func: argument,
MV3 event pages, and promise-returning permissions.request all predate
115, but 115 is the current ESR floor and is where this was verified.
What is NOT here, and cannot be: an extension ID that Atlas's RPC server
could pin in its CORS allowlist. A Firefox extension's page origin is
moz-extension://<uuid>, where the uuid is generated per INSTALLATION, not
per add-on. electron/rpc/extensionServer.js therefore accepts the
moz-extension scheme by shape and leans on the X-Atlas-Token pairing secret
as the actual authorization boundary, which it already was.
Host permissions are optional-by-default under Gecko MV3: they are listed
below but not granted at install. popup.js detects that and offers a grant
button; see the permissionBox block in popup.html.
name: Atlas Browser Extension
author: Atlas Developer
description: Integration between visual novel forums and Atlas Desktop Game Manager
